analysis.title: China: October activity data broadly weakened, pointing to a soft start to Q4
key_insights: China's October activity data weakened from September and missed consensus on industrial production, fixed asset investment and retail sales. Goldman reads this as a soft start to Q4 with a wide gap between strong exports and subdued domestic demand.

Industrial production grew 4.8% yoy in October versus 5.5% in September (GS forecast 5.0%, consensus 5.3%). Slower output in autos and ferrous metal smelting more than offset faster output in computer and other equipment manufacturing. GS estimates output fell 0.3% mom sa non-annualized.

On a single-month basis, GS estimates fixed asset investment fell 16.3% yoy in October versus -7.2% in September, despite a low base. Year-to-date FAI was -8.1% yoy versus the GS forecast of -6.9% and consensus of -7.0%. GS attributes the drop to slower government spending of previously raised funds.

FAI declines were broad-based by sector in October: manufacturing -9.5% yoy (from -1.0%), infrastructure -18.5% (from -11.6%), property -33.6% (from -26.2%) and other investment -17.5% (from +3.7%). GS cautions that NBS statistical corrections to previously overstated data may have amplified reported volatility, and the drop looks larger than steel and cement output would imply.

Nominal retail sales grew 0.4% yoy in October versus 1.1% in September (GS forecast 0.5%, consensus 0.8%). Online goods sales fell 3.5% yoy and restaurant revenue rose 0.7%. GS thinks the earlier Mid-Autumn Festival pulled some consumption into September.

Retail category detail: communication appliance sales slowed to +6.5% yoy from +31.1%, food to +0.5% from +6.7%, clothing to -2.0% from +1.2%, and autos stayed weak at -21.4%. Gasoline sales value rose 4.4% on a 24% rise in retail fuel prices, while GS estimates volume fell 19% yoy.
The Services Industry Output Index, which tracks tertiary GDP (58% of the economy in 2025), slowed to 4.6% yoy in October from 4.8% in September. GS estimates it rose 0.2% mom sa.

Property activity stayed weak. Sales by floor space fell 19.0% yoy, new starts fell 18.2%, completions fell 39.3%, and real estate investment fell 33.6%. NBS and private data show early home-price stabilization in some large cities, while most lower-tier cities remain under downward pressure.

The labor market was broadly stable. Surveyed unemployment was 5.1% nationwide and in 31 major cities, down from 5.2%. Youth (16-24) unemployment eased to 18.0% in September from 18.9% in August. GS warns the revised definition may understate stress among young workers, given weak domestic demand and AI pressure on entry-level white-collar jobs.

GS keeps its forecast that sequential real GDP growth slows to 4.0% qoq annualized in Q4 from 4.9% in Q3. With this year's growth target nearly secured, GS expects some government funds raised in Q4 may be deployed in Q1 next year to support 2027 growth.
GS Asia-MAP activity scores for October were -5 for industrial production, -10 for fixed asset investment and 0 for retail sales.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Output growth slowed and missed expectations, led by autos and ferrous metals, despite still-solid exports.
Investment weakened more than expected, with declines across manufacturing, infrastructure, property and other investment.

macro_indicators.indicator: China fixed asset investment, single month (yoy)
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS-derived single-month figure. The sharp drop likely reflects slower government spending of previously raised funds, and may be exaggerated by NBS statistical corrections.
Consumption slowed and missed expectations, partly because the earlier Mid-Autumn Festival shifted spending into September.
Services output, a close proxy for tertiary GDP growth, moderated slightly.
Labor market conditions were broadly stable. GS estimates the seasonally adjusted rate was unchanged at 5.2%.
Property investment contraction deepened, and sales, starts and completions also stayed deeply negative.
GS expects a sequential slowdown in Q4 and maintains this forecast after the October data.

risk_factors: Reported FAI volatility may be amplified by occasional NBS statistical corrections to previously overstated data.
Sequential figures are highly sensitive to the seasonal adjustment methodology, and NBS and GS estimates of monthly changes differ.
Weak domestic demand and AI adoption may be adding pressure on entry-level white-collar jobs, which the revised youth unemployment definition may understate.
Most lower-tier cities remain under downward pressure on home prices.
geopolitical: Sulfuric acid output stayed subdued at -8.6% yoy in October (September -12.4%), which GS attributes to continued disruptions from the Middle East conflict.
